debts.claim: Product-law matching's domain condition is too weak. 'A product operation exists and the size parameter is additive' is satisfied literally by disjoint union, which moves BOTH coordinates of a two-parameter family, so target and bound can differ with no board change available. Every case the diagnostic gets right is a single-parameter family; its one false positive is the two-parameter one.
debts.action: A candidate repair (require the operation to preserve the family's full parameterisation) is stated and DELIBERATELY NOT ADOPTED, because it was derived from the item it would exclude. It needs items chosen by someone who has not seen the adjudication, including two-parameter families where the board DID change.

debts.claim: The five-category law vocabulary cannot express 'the right law, degraded by a log'. Rater B declined to fire on case 4 (Kadison-Singer) by reading the matrix-Chernoff penalty that way, which is arguably exactly what that board did.
debts.action: Do NOT add a category reflexively — the standing rule is that catalogues shrink before they grow. Decide first whether the gap explains other divergences; if it explains only case 4, it is a property of that case, not of the vocabulary.

debts.claim: The retrospective arm cannot measure a diagnostic's value. A rule-less rater given the same item scored J = 1.000 (5/5 positives, 8/8 negatives) against product-law matching's 0.675, a lift of -0.325, with a recognition probe of 13/13.
debts.action: Nothing to fix; this is a property of retrospective cases, not a bug. What it CHANGES: no retrospective 2x2 in this tree may be quoted as evidence that a diagnostic works. The prospective arm is now the only instrument that can answer the question, and this is the third independent measurement saying so (step D 100%, L2 5-of-5, this 13/13).

debts.claim: The benchmark cannot evaluate any criterion about success versus failure, because all 13 P1 cases are successes. The negative twins are negatives about the TIGHTNESS of a bound, not about moves that failed.
debts.action: Needs a corpus of FAILED board changes — attempts that changed the board and did not work. The seed flagged survivorship selection as blocking PPV estimates; this is the second distinct thing it blocks. Collecting failed attempts is harder than collecting famous successes and is the main thing that would make the benchmark able to test a criterion rather than merely fit one.

debts.claim: Product-law matching is UNDEFINED where the feasible set is not closed under the product operation. For the hypercube problem the constraint is a density threshold and density is multiplicative, so the product of two extremal examples is a quarter of the cube, not half: there is no product of extremal examples to read a target law off. Case 1 and N9 are removed from the domain.
debts.action: The obvious patch -- require closure -- is NOT adopted, because it was derived from the item it excludes. Note this is the SECOND such patch (D23 was the first, from N8). Two post-hoc patches from two items is the signature of a rule being fitted rather than tested; a third should be read as a refutation, not a repair.

debts.claim: The rule 'does the best known lower bound match the upper bound to within a constant factor?' reproduces product-law matching's verdicts on the hypercube boards exactly, needs no product-law machinery, and is immune to the rater dispute over the counting board's label. Verified: the l2-vs-max distinction can carry at most a factor sqrt(2), and it was being used to flag a polynomial (log n vs sqrt n) gap.
debts.action: RUN. d28_bound_strength.json + BASELINE.md. The one-line test 'is the bound tight to within a constant factor?' scores J = +0.750 against product-law matching's +0.607, with ZERO false positives where the diagnostic takes one, and differs on exactly one item — N8, where the diagnostic is wrong. The product-law machinery is SURPLUS: more complicated, worse-performing, and needing two post-hoc domain patches the one-line test does not need. Both lose to the rule-less rater (+1.000). What survives of the rebuild is D20's field kappa and the falsifications themselves, not the rule.

debts.where: p3-taxonomy/taxonomy.json -> level_axis; p1-retrodiction/heldout/*.json and controls/*.json -> level; p1-retrodiction/tools/assign_levels.py, tools/level_audit.py
debts.claim: The catalogue has no axis for WHAT LEVEL and IN WHAT SUBSTRATE a change occurred. Two independent signs: (a) Zhang changed the equidistribution board one level DOWN while leaving the GPY sieve unchanged, so 7b is a level-(n-1) board change feeding an unchanged level-n board; (b) Pierce sec. 8.5 argues efficient congruencing and l^2 decoupling share rescaling, multilinear estimates, iteration and transversality, quoting Wooley that they may be 'p-adic and Archimedean perspectives of one unified method' -- a same-mechanism-two-substrates claim about a case the taxonomy calls a board change, made by the survey author rather than by us.
debts.action: THE AXIS IS ENCODED, as an axis and not as a sixth transformation -- the transformation vocabulary is untouched and still closed. Six values, every one instantiated except `unclear`, which is deliberately kept unused so a later encoder is not forced to choose (a forced label is what produced kappa = 0.048). All 17 scoreable items carry it: 10 same-level, 3 none (the controls 14, 15, 17), 2 reduction-level (cases 6 and 11), 1 substrate (case 9), 1 input-level (control 16 -- the item the axis exists for). tools/validate.py now FAILS the tree on a missing or invalid axis and on any control marked same-level, and the gate was negative-tested. The level cannot leak: it is in the held-out half, FORBIDDEN_IN_BEFORE covers it, and pack.py builds items from an allowlist. WHAT THE FULL PASS SHOWS, none of it visible from control 16 alone: (a) the corpus is 10 of 13 same-level and the ONLY input-level item is a control, so the axis is nearly constant on the positives and cannot discriminate on its own -- it must not be sold as if it could; (b) case 7a and control 16 are EXACT COMPLEMENTS on the axis, which is why that pair works; (c) case 13's old board CONSUMED case 10's object, and Dinur's same-level change ELIMINATED that level rather than improving it -- one instance, so no axis value was added for it. STILL OPEN BECAUSE IT IS UNVALIDATED. The assignments are mine alone, single-encoder, exactly like the v0 labels. The only reason to expect better than 0.048 is D20's split: closed-vocabulary FIELDS reproduced at +0.811 and +0.755 where the rule did not, and this is a field. Reason for optimism, not evidence. The test is the D20 instrument over these 17 items with raters who have not read taxonomy.json -- one field, so cheaper than D20. Cases 6 and 11 are at MEDIUM confidence on the same-level/reduction-level boundary and are the first two to ask about.

debts.claim: The case 7 split gives the benchmark its FIRST CONTEMPORANEOUS WITHIN-PROBLEM CONTROL: 7a (Maynard-Tao, board changed) against 16 (Zhang, level-n board unchanged) -- one problem, one year, two teams, with the counterfactual actually run. Every other positive/control comparison in P1 is cross-problem and confounded by difficulty.
debts.why_it_matters: D25 measured that a rule-less rater ceilings the benchmark at J = 1.000 with 13/13 recognition -- it only has to NAME the problem. A contemporaneous within-problem pair is the one structure recall cannot crack: both halves are 'bounded prime gaps, 2013', so the rater must separate Maynard-Tao from Zhang ON MECHANISM. This is the most promising response to D25 that does not require waiting for the prospective arm.
debts.action: STILL NOT RUN, and now with a number saying why that is right. tools/pair_power.py: each pair is one binary decision at chance 1/2, so an exact one-sided sign test needs FIVE pairs scored perfectly to clear alpha = 0.05 (p = 0.0312) and EIGHT to survive one miss (p = 0.0352; at n = 7 one miss gives 0.0625 and fails). One discrimination pair is in hand. CANDIDATES RANKED in PAIRS.md, every claim recalled rather than sourced, each with the document that would settle it and the way it might fail: (1) sunflower 2019, Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang against Rao weeks later on the new board -- two teams, one season, and NEITHER half is a failure, which is what makes it the best candidate; (2) bounded gaps extended to a triple with Polymath8a/8b, which would put board change, level-(n-1) change and better play on ONE problem and is the sharpest test of D30's level axis; (3) matrix multiplication 2021-2023, where refinement versus new mechanism is genuinely contested; (4) Spencer constructive, recorded as PARALLEL BOARDS and explicitly not a pair; (5) strong parallel repetition 2008, not a pair -- it is a twin and already is one. Cap set 2016 and sphere packing 2016 are REJECTED as pairs with reasons, so they are not proposed again. ONE PAIR IS AVAILABLE NOW WITH NO NEW SOURCE: Roth 2023, Kelley-Meka against Bloom-Sisask days later on the same board, both must-not-fire. It does NOT count toward the five -- with no 'which is which' there is nothing to score -- but it measures specificity inside one problem-period and the authors' own words make the encoding clean. THE HONEST ARITHMETIC, stated in PAIRS.md rather than buried: one pair in hand, four candidates, at most three of which survive their stated risks, against a floor of five. This route does not reach the floor on current material. It is still the cheaper route to be wrong about -- a failed candidate costs one transcript, a failed prospective prediction costs months.

debts.claim: THE BENCHMARK'S SUBJECT MATTER, STATED BY THE PEOPLE ON THE BOARD, CONTEMPORANEOUSLY. Bloom-Sisask write that an exponent of 1/3, 'or perhaps even 1/4', 'seems to be the limit of any argument that uses any sort of "density increment" argument with Bohr sets (whether using Kelley-Meka ideas or a more traditional Fourier analytic approach)', while Behrend's construction puts the truth at 1/2. So the density-increment board has a ceiling below the known answer, and the interval (1/3, 1/2] in the exponent is unreachable from it on the practitioners' own account.
debts.why_it_matters: Every leak in P1's retrospective corpus is one WE identified after the board was left, which is the contamination D25 showed the retrospective arm cannot escape: a rater who recognises the problem already knows the answer. This is a leak identified BEFORE the board was left, in print, by the people playing on it, with a number attached. That is the shape of item the prospective arm is trying to manufacture, and here the literature supplies one for free.
debts.action: INSTRUMENT BUILT, and it already holds TWO instances rather than the one anecdote this debt was opened on. (1) Roth/density-increment-with-Bohr-sets, STATED-BY-AUTHORS, OPEN: cap 1/3 against a truth of 1/2 that Behrend's construction proves, with the authors' prediction sealed. (2) GPY/one-dimensional-sieve, DERIVED-FROM-PRIMARY, RESOLVED as held-and-board-left: rho_k(F) saturates at 4 for every k, so under Bombieri-Vinogradov the criterion caps at exactly the value it must exceed, and the advance came twice by leaving a board -- Maynard-Tao leaving the sieve, Zhang leaving the equidistribution board one level down (D30). The second instance was already in the repository and cost no new source. WHAT THE TWO INSTANCES TAUGHT, none of it anticipated when this debt was written: a cap can be an UNATTAINED SUPREMUM (so the tool allows cap == truth with cap_attained false and a boundary note, rather than fudging 3.999); the truth a cap falls short of may be a CONJECTURE rather than a theorem, which is a second axis in the record; a resolution must state the LEVEL at which a board changed, because Zhang beat the requirement without touching the capped sieve; and NEITHER diagnostic covers both instances -- product-law matching is silent on Roth (no product structure in [N]) while the D28 one-line test fires, and the D28 test has nothing to read on GPY because the cap is on a criterion rather than on a bound against a construction. STILL OPEN AND THIS IS THE WORK: two items are an instrument, not a measurement. Four candidates are named in CEILINGS.md with the one document each needs (Selberg's parity problem; a pre-2020 statement of the logarithmic barrier; the n/2 barrier for bush/hairbrush in F_q^n; the laser method's proved limit for omega, which would need a PROVED evidence tier that is deliberately not added until an instance arrives). Do not add tiers or entries without a source reached in-session.

debts.claim: The per-source `verified` flags inside the ITEM files are not linked to citations.json and have gone stale: 27 of 56 source entries across cases, twins and controls still say verified: false while the citation layer carries 32 VERIFIED claims. Found by reconciling control 14, whose three sources all said verified: false while row C14 stood VERIFIED and ADJ-14 had been adjudicated on them.
debts.why_it_matters: The item file is what a scorer or a rater is handed; citations.json is what the verification pass wrote. A rater reading 'verified: false' on a source that has in fact been checked is being shown the wrong provenance, and the direction of this error is the flattering one for the verification pass and the unflattering one for the items.
debts.action: DONE, and the sweep it warned against was avoided: every one of the 55 per-source flags now carries `citation_row` (or null), `tier` and `basis`, decided cite by cite against the row that does or does not cover it. 43 read verified, 12 do not. 13 flags moved false -> true, NONE moved the other way, so the drift was entirely in the direction that understated the verification pass. The invariant is ONE-DIRECTIONAL on purpose: verified: true requires a linked row whose status is VERIFIED or CORRECTED, while verified: false beside a VERIFIED row is legitimate and now must say which NEIGHBOURING claim the row covers instead -- three do, and they are the interesting ones (row C13 verifies Dinur 2007, not Arora-Safra; row C4 verifies that NOBODY states the threshold attached to Weaver; row C12 is about Perelman's entropy, not Hamilton's programme). WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND THAT WAS NOT THE ORIGINAL COMPLAINT: three twins (N10, N14, N15) read verified on a DECLARED basis with no citations.json row at all, and they were never among the eight STANDARD twins D21 tracked -- so how they came to be flagged verified is unrecorded. Left standing and labelled, not quietly downgraded; the generated caveat in DEBTS.md names them. Also: eight flags now read tier NONE, meaning no row covers them -- that list is the honest version of what was previously 27 undifferentiated falses. The before-board schema now requires citation_row and basis; twins and controls have no schema, so for them the checker is the only enforcement.
